arguments.decision_needed: The tenant reports the landlord's LG washing machine (there when they moved in) has failed with a power fault and says it can't be fixed. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would remain their property and be taken with them when they leave. Please tell us: (1) do you consent to the tenant fitting their own machine; (2) who pays to disconnect and remove the old machine and fit the new one; (3) what should happen to your existing machine (inspect, repair, dispose); (4) may the tenant's machine stay connected. Alternatively we can send our contractor to inspect/repair yours.
options: Our contractor inspects/repairs the landlord's machine first (recommended if you wish to keep supplying one)
Consent to tenant's own machine; state who pays removal/fitting and what happens to the old machine
Landlord arranges own contractor/replacement
Decline

arguments.body: Hello, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Fitting your own machine needs the landlord's consent, so we've put your offer to them, including that it would stay yours and go with you when you leave. We've also asked who covers removing the old machine and fitting the new one, and what happens to the old one. Please don't remove or dispose of the existing machine until we come back to you. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you once we have the landlord's answer, and by 30 July at the latest.

arguments.note: Tenant's own appliance request, not a repair. Tenant's machine would stay theirs, not on the inventory, taken when they leave. Landlord asked re consent, who pays disconnect/removal/fit, fate of landlord's LG. Tenant's claim that it can't be fixed is unverified (own Google research).

arguments.decision_needed: The tenant reports the landlord's LG washing machine (there when they moved in) has failed with a power fault and says it can't be fixed. They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would remain their property and be taken with them when they leave. Please tell us: (1) do you consent to the tenant fitting their own machine; (2) who pays to disconnect and remove the old machine and fit the new one; (3) what should happen to your existing machine (inspect, repair, dispose); (4) may the tenant's machine stay connected. Alternatively we can send our contractor to inspect/repair yours.
options: Our contractor inspects/repairs the landlord's machine first (recommended if you wish to keep supplying one)
Consent to tenant's own machine; state who pays removal/fitting and what happens to the old machine
Landlord arranges own contractor/replacement
Decline

arguments.body: Hello, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Fitting your own machine needs the landlord's consent, so we've put your offer to them, including that it would stay yours and go with you when you leave. We've also asked who covers removing the old machine and fitting the new one, and what happens to the old one. Please don't remove or dispose of the existing machine until we come back to you. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you once we have the landlord's answer, and by 30 July at the latest.

arguments.note: Tenant's own appliance request, not a repair. Tenant's machine would stay theirs, not on the inventory, taken when they leave. Landlord asked re consent, who pays disconnect/removal/fit, fate of landlord's LG. Tenant's claim that it can't be fixed is unverified (own Google research).
